text:
anya: quick heads-up — in canary perf this morning I saw a 5x spike in KV evictions for multi-edit sessions (long prompt churn). looks like fragmentation + low reuse, not simple TTL churn.
chris: link to the flamegraph and eviction chart: https://grafana.redwood/prod/d/WXYZ/kv-evict?view=canary
miguel: can you paste a couple of example keys? curious if we are not normalizing prefixes so identical semantic prefixes miss the cache
anya: here are a few stripped logs from the canary (anonymized):
```
KV_TOUCH key="user:987|prefix:How to refactor   \nthis code?" size=48 miss
KV_TOUCH key="user:987|prefix:How to refactor this code?" size=47 hit
KV_EVICT key="user:987|prefix:How to refactor    this code?" reason=mem_pressure
KV_PAGE_ALLOC pages=12 resident=840kb
```
anya: note the extra whitespace & punctuation differences causing separate entries. Also saw many very long keys (>512 bytes) that force different indexing paths and increase fragmentation.
sasha: that matches my local repro — we generate keys straight from raw prompt slices + session id. we should canonicalize (trim, collapse whitespace, normalize punctuation) before keying, and cap key length with a stable hash suffix.
chris: +1. also worried about backpressure: when many requests create slightly different keys we bloom the index and trigger page splits. propose a two-prong canary: 1) key canonicalization & truncation+hash 2) adaptive prefetch throttling that rejects prefetches when page-split rate > threshold.
miguel: suggested canonicalizer (pseudo):
```python
import re, hashlib

def canonical_key(prefix, user_id, prompt_hash):
    p = prefix.strip().lower()
    p = re.sub(r"\\s+", " ", p)
    p = re.sub(r"[.,;:!]+$", "", p)  # trim trailing punctuation
    short = hashlib.sha1(p.encode()).hexdigest()[:12]
    return f"{user_id}|{prompt_hash}|{short}"
```
chris: looks reasonable. also add a metric for key_cardinality_by_tenant so we can detect tenants that blow up the index.
anya: profiling numbers: before change page-split-rate=0.02 -> after high-churn tests 0.12, eviction_rate from 0.8% to 4.5%, resident_pages grew 30% over 30m in long-ctx runs.
sasha: for prefetch/backpressure idea: make prefetch opt-in per-session and add a token-bucket limiter that shares capacity across a worker. if token bucket exhausted, fall back to on-demand (no prefetch). reduces write amplification.
miguel: we should also consider periodic compaction: merge neighbouring small pages when fragmentation > 0.6 to reduce memory blowup. compaction is async and rate-limited.
chris: rollout plan: small canary on dedicated infra: enable canonical_key + truncation for 5% traffic, enable key_cardinality alert (pager if >100k new keys/5m for tenant), enable prefetch token-bucket with permissive limits. collect eviction_rate, page_split_rate, resident_pages, hit_rate.
deploy-bot: canary deploy started: canary/id=kv-keynorm-2024-05, targets=eng-runtime-canary-3, time=1716606000
anya: I'll instrument and run the long-ctx k6 load (script kv_longctx_10k) against canary tomorrow morning.
sasha: I'll land the canonicalizer patch and add unit tests for whitespace/punc edgecases.
miguel: I'll prototype page compaction toggle behind feature flag — low risk.
chris: SGTM. ping here when canary metrics land. if we still see high fragmentation we'll try a short-lived aggressive TTL for new keys (60s) and warm frequently used prefixes to reduce churn. :thumbsup:
